hypothesis: A minimal, containerized AI localization pipeline that combines deterministic language detection, MT/LLM translation with glossary hints, and basic automated QA (length, placeholder, and tag checks) can process a small but realistic enterprise content set end-to-end with zero hard failures (crashes, unhandled exceptions) and produce structurally valid outputs (no broken placeholders/tags) suitable for human review exports in at least two target languages.

baseline.description: A simple, linear localization script that reads English source strings from a CSV, calls a generic MT/LLM API for translation without terminology support, performs no automated structural QA, and writes a raw CSV of translations without any TMS-compatible segmentation or metadata.

key_characteristics.architecture: Single Python script, no modular package structure, no config files; direct in-code constants for file paths and API keys.
key_characteristics.content_handling: Assumes all input is English; no language detection or mixed-language handling.
key_characteristics.translation: Single MT/LLM provider, called with plain source text and target language; no glossary, no TM, no retries, no rate-limit handling.
key_characteristics.qa_checks: None beyond implicit API errors; does not check for length ratio, placeholder preservation, or tag integrity.
key_characteristics.export_format: Flat CSV with columns: id, source, target_<lang_code>; no segmentation, no per-locale files, no status fields.
key_characteristics.observability: Console logging only; no structured logs or run IDs.
key_characteristics.reproducibility: No containerization; no pinned dependencies; environment setup is ad hoc.

repository_mapping.notes: This baseline is primarily a pedagogical foil; it may be included in the repo as an anti-pattern example but is not the primary subject of this experiment.

treatment.description: A baseline but production-shaped AI localization pipeline implemented as a small Python package and CLI, with explicit stages for content ingestion, language detection, MT/LLM-based translation with terminology hints, basic automated QA checks, and export of outputs in a TMS-like format. The pipeline is containerized, environment-pinned, and designed to be reproducible on a sample dataset.

key_characteristics.architecture: Modular Python package with clear stage boundaries: ingest -> detect_language -> translate -> qa -> export. Configuration via YAML; separate data, config, and code directories.
key_characteristics.content_handling: Ingestion from CSV/JSON files with fields: id, source_text, source_locale, content_type, placeholders, tags. Language detection stage verifies or infers source language for each record, flagging inconsistencies.
key_characteristics.translation: Pluggable translation backend with a default provider (e.g., OpenAI or generic MT API) called through a single adapter interface. Terminology support via glossary hints injected into prompts or provider-specific glossary parameters. Deterministic settings where possible (temperature, top_p).
key_characteristics.qa_checks: Length ratio checks (target/source within configurable bounds per locale), placeholder integrity checks (all required placeholders present and unaltered), and HTML/XML tag balance checks (no unclosed or mismatched tags). Items failing QA are marked with status and QA error codes.
key_characteristics.export_format: TMS-like CSV or TSV with columns including: segment_id, source_locale, target_locale, source_text, target_text, content_type, qa_status, qa_issues, glossary_applied, run_id, created_at. Optionally, XLIFF-like JSON for future extension.
key_characteristics.observability: Structured logging (JSON lines) with per-run UUID, stage timings, and error summaries written to logs/ directory.
key_characteristics.reproducibility: Dockerfile, requirements.txt/pyproject.toml, and a deterministic configuration file (YAML). External MT/LLM provider and models are declared in config, not hard-coded.

workloads.name: sample_customer_support_tickets
workloads.description: A small but realistic set of anonymized English customer support ticket snippets for a SaaS product, including UI references, placeholders, and simple markup. Chosen for medium risk and high structural variety.

input_schema.source_text: string; may include placeholders like {user_name}, {product_name}, and simple HTML tags <b>, <i>, <a>
input_schema.metadata: optional JSON-encoded string for future extension (e.g., 'risk_level', 'channel')

special_features: 5–10% of content includes inline HTML tags.
A small subset (e.g., 5–10 segments) intentionally includes mixed-language elements (English with isolated Spanish or French terms) to test language detection robustness.

workloads.name: sample_marketing_snippets
workloads.description: Short marketing and product UI snippets for a regulated B2B SaaS product, focusing on segmentation and tag handling rather than high domain risk.

input_schema.source_text: string; UI and marketing snippets, including line breaks and occasionally markdown-like formatting (e.g., **bold**).

special_features: Designed to verify that short and long segments both pass through the pipeline cleanly.
Some strings include non-breaking spaces or unusual punctuation to test tag/placeholder parsing robustness.

fixed_parameters.mt_llm_provider: Configured via environment variable and YAML (e.g., OPENAI or GENERIC_MT_API), but fixed for a given experiment run.
fixed_parameters.mt_model: Single model ID per experiment (e.g., 'gpt-4.1-mini' or 'generic-mt-v1'); no dynamic model switching.
fixed_parameters.glossary_application_mode: Soft enforcement via prompt or provider glossary hints; same glossary for all segments in a given run.

randomness_and_seeding.mt_llm_determinism: Use deterministic settings (temperature=0, top_p=1); note that some external providers may still be nondeterministic across calls or time.
randomness_and_seeding.ordering: Process segments in ascending id order to ensure reproducible ordering of outputs.

environmental_controls.container: All primary runs executed inside the provided Docker image built from ch05_baseline_pipeline/Dockerfile.
environmental_controls.dependency_lock: requirements.txt or equivalent lock file committed in the repo, installed at image build time.

resource_limits.cpu: At least 2 vCPUs available to container
resource_limits.memory: At least 4 GiB RAM available to container

environmental_controls.network: Outbound HTTPS access to chosen MT/LLM provider; otherwise no special connectivity requirements.

dataset_versioning.immutability: Input datasets used for experiments must not be modified in-place; any change requires a new dataset_tag and associated experiment_id.

metrics.name: segments_total
metrics.description: Total number of input segments passed into the pipeline for a given run (per dataset and per target locale).

metrics.name: segments_successfully_translated
metrics.description: Number of segments for which a target text was generated without API or internal processing errors.

metrics.name: segments_failed_translation
metrics.description: Number of segments for which translation could not be produced (e.g., API error, timeout, unrecoverable exception).

metrics.name: segments_passing_all_qa
metrics.description: Number of translated segments that pass all automated QA checks (length ratio, placeholder integrity, tag integrity).

metrics.name: segments_failing_any_qa
metrics.description: Number of translated segments that fail one or more QA checks and are flagged for human review or remediation.

metrics.name: qa_failure_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of translated segments that fail at least one QA check: segments_failing_any_qa / segments_successfully_translated.

metrics.name: placeholder_integrity_violation_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of translated segments that fail placeholder integrity checks (missing, altered, or additional placeholders) among those that contain placeholders in the source.

metrics.name: tag_integrity_violation_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of translated segments that fail HTML/XML tag integrity checks (unbalanced or mismatched tags) among those containing tags in the source.

metrics.name: length_ratio_out_of_bounds_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of translated segments where the target-to-source character length ratio falls outside configured bounds for that language pair.

metrics.name: pipeline_end_to_end_time
metrics.description: Wall-clock time from pipeline start (after environment ready) to completion of export for all target locales for a given workload.

metrics.name: avg_translation_latency_per_segment
metrics.description: Average latency measured only for the translation stage per segment (including retries).

metrics.name: hard_failure_indicator
metrics.description: Binary indicator of whether any unhandled exception or crash occurred that prevented completion of the pipeline for a given run.

primary.name: no_hard_failures
primary.criterion: hard_failure_indicator == false for all workloads and target locales in at least three independent runs (fresh containers, same config).
primary.rationale: Baseline pipeline must be robust enough to complete jobs consistently without crashes.

primary.name: structural_integrity
primary.criterion: placeholder_integrity_violation_rate <= 0.02 and tag_integrity_violation_rate <= 0.02 for each workload-target_locale combination.
primary.rationale: Even a baseline must preserve structural elements (placeholders and tags) nearly perfectly to be usable by enterprise teams.

secondary.name: manageable_qa_failure_rate
secondary.rationale: The baseline pipeline should not overwhelm human reviewers with excessive QA failures; ~85% clean pass is a reasonable initial target.

secondary.name: completion_time_expectation
secondary.criterion: pipeline_end_to_end_time <= 300 seconds for 150-segment workloads across both target locales combined, on the reference hardware.
secondary.rationale: Ensures that the baseline is fast enough to be practical in interactive development and small-batch testing contexts.

interpretation_notes: If structural integrity thresholds are not met while language quality appears reasonable, the next iteration should prioritize improvements in placeholder and tag handling over model tuning.
If qa_failure_rate is driven primarily by length ratio violations rather than structural errors, reviewers may decide to relax bounds or differentiate by content_type.

failure_modes.name: api_instability_or_rate_limits
failure_modes.description: External MT/LLM provider returns intermittent errors, timeouts, or rate-limit responses, causing segments_failed_translation to spike or causing hard_failure_indicator to flip to true.
failure_modes.detection: Increased segments_failed_translation count; structured logs showing HTTP 429/5xx patterns; pipeline abort logs.
mitigations: Implement exponential backoff and bounded retries in the translation adapter.
Allow batch size and concurrency controls to be configured in YAML.
Offer a dry-run mode that stops before translation for quick structural checks of ingestion and QA logic.

failure_modes.name: incorrect_language_detection
failure_modes.description: Language detection misclassifies some segments, leading to incorrect translation routing (e.g., treating an already-Spanish snippet as English).
failure_modes.detection: Compare detected language codes against known source_locale where available; count mismatches; flag segments where detection_confidence < threshold.
mitigations: For Ch.05 baseline, keep detection simple but configurable: allow bypass when source_locale is trusted.
Log all detection mismatches and include them as qa_issues for potential human review, but do not block pipeline completion.

failure_modes.name: placeholder_parsing_errors
failure_modes.description: Placeholder regex or parser fails to correctly identify placeholders, either missing valid ones or hallucinating placeholders from normal text.
failure_modes.detection: Manual spot checks of qa_issues labeled 'placeholder_missing' or 'placeholder_extra'; unit tests on synthetic strings; unexpectedly high placeholder_integrity_violation_rate.
mitigations: Use explicit placeholder patterns (e.g., {SNAKE_CASE} or {camelCase}) and document constraints in the dataset description.
Implement unit tests for placeholder extraction logic under tests/ subdirectory.
Log the list of extracted placeholders per segment for debugging.

failure_modes.name: html_tag_validation_false_positives
failure_modes.description: The tag integrity checker flags benign differences (e.g., whitespace or attribute order changes) as errors.
failure_modes.detection: High tag_integrity_violation_rate with visually correct translations; log samples where violations occur; manual inspection.
mitigations: Restrict baseline to simple tag sets (<b>, <i>, <a>) and perform structural rather than byte-level comparison.
Normalize whitespace and attribute ordering before comparison where feasible.
Document current limitations and defer complex markup handling to later chapters.

failure_modes.name: non_reproducible_results_across_runs
failure_modes.description: Same configuration and dataset produce materially different results across runs (e.g., different placeholder errors, large swings in qa_failure_rate).
failure_modes.detection: Run the same workload-target combination at least three times and compare metrics and sample outputs; check for config drift or unpinned dependencies.
mitigations: Ensure deterministic settings for the MT/LLM provider to the extent supported.
Pin dependency versions strictly and rebuild the Docker image before each experiment series.
Persist config and model identifiers in the run metadata and export schema.

software.os: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 LTS recommended) or equivalent container base image
software.dependencies: Installed via `pip install -r requirements.txt` inside the Docker image. Likely libraries include: requests or httpx, pydantic, pyyaml, pandas, langdetect or fasttext-based detector, lxml or html5lib for tag parsing, loguru or stdlib logging, click or typer for CLI.
software.container_runtime: Docker Engine 20.x or higher (or compatible, such as Podman, with minor modifications).

services.mt_llm_provider: At least one MT/LLM API, e.g., OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or a generic SaaS MT provider. The specific provider, base URL, and model ID must be documented in config.
services.network: Outbound HTTPS connectivity from the container to the MT/LLM provider endpoint.

credentials.api_keys: Environment variables such as MT_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY set either directly or via docker --env-file (see .env.example).
credentials.secrets_handling: No secrets committed to the repository; .env.example documents required keys and expected names.

hardware_reference.storage: At least 2 GiB free disk space for images, logs, and outputs.
hardware_reference.notes: The small dataset sizes keep hardware requirements modest; metrics are relative to this reference environment.

run_instructions:
Clone the repository:
  git clone https://github.com/bookauthority/ai-localization-quality-culture-compliance.git
  cd ai-localization-quality-culture-compliance/ch05_baseline_pipeline

Inspect the sample datasets and glossary:
  ls data/
  # e.g., sample_customer_support_en.csv, sample_marketing_snippets_en.csv, glossary_en_es_fr.csv

Review and, if needed, adapt the baseline configuration file (do not change dataset file names or structure for this experiment):
  cat config/baseline_en_to_es_fr.yml
  # Key fields: mt_provider, mt_model, target_locales, qa.length_ratio_bounds, paths.input_file, paths.output_dir, paths.log_dir.

Create an environment file with API credentials based on .env.example:
  cp .env.example .env
  # Edit .env to include your MT/LLM provider API keys and endpoints.

Build the Docker image for the baseline pipeline:
  docker build -t ailoc-ch05-baseline:latest .

Run the baseline pipeline for the primary workload (customer support tickets) inside the container:
  docker run --rm \
    --env-file .env \
    -v "$(pwd)/outputs":/app/outputs \
    -v "$(pwd)/logs":/app/logs \
    ailoc-ch05-baseline:latest \
    python run_pipeline.py \
      --config config/baseline_en_to_es_fr.yml \
      --input data/sample_customer_support_en.csv \
      --workload-name sample_customer_support_tickets

Optionally, run the pipeline for the secondary workload (marketing snippets):
  docker run --rm \
    --env-file .env \
    -v "$(pwd)/outputs":/app/outputs \
    -v "$(pwd)/logs":/app/logs \
    ailoc-ch05-baseline:latest \
    python run_pipeline.py \
      --config config/baseline_en_to_es_fr.yml \
      --input data/sample_marketing_snippets_en.csv \
      --workload-name sample_marketing_snippets

For each run, locate the outputs and logs:
  ls outputs/
  # Expect files such as: sample_customer_support_tickets_es-ES.csv, sample_customer_support_tickets_fr-FR.csv
  ls logs/
  # Expect logs with run IDs and JSONL structured entries, e.g., run_2026-01-10T12-34-56Z.jsonl

Extract experiment metrics from logs using the provided helper script (if implemented) or manual inspection:
  # If helper exists:
  python tools/summarize_run_metrics.py --logs logs/run_*.jsonl --output outputs/metrics_summary.json
  # Otherwise, inspect logs for per-run metrics blocks, and manually compute metrics such as qa_failure_rate and violation rates.

Repeat the entire pipeline run (steps 6–9) at least two more times with the same configuration and datasets to assess reproducibility. Compare metrics across runs to validate that hard_failure_indicator remains false and key rates (placeholder_integrity_violation_rate, tag_integrity_violation_rate, qa_failure_rate) are stable.

Export outputs for human review in a TMS-like format (this may already be the default CSV structure). Verify that the exported files include per-segment fields: segment_id, source_locale, target_locale, source_text, target_text, qa_status, qa_issues, and run_id. Archive these files under a directory named with experiment_id and dataset_tag for later chapters.

run_record.description: Top-level record capturing a single execution of the baseline pipeline for a given workload and configuration.

run_id.description: UUID or timestamp-based identifier generated at run start.

timestamp_utc.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for when the run started.

git_commit_hash.description: Short or full hash of the repository commit used for the run.

dataset_tag.description: Logical label for the dataset version used (e.g., 'ch05-baseline-v1').

config_path.description: Path to the YAML configuration file used for the run.

mt_provider.description: Identifier for the MT/LLM provider used (e.g., 'openai', 'generic_mt').

metrics.description: Aggregate metrics for the run, potentially broken down by target_locale.

outputs_manifest.description: List of generated output files and their metadata.

segment_record.description: Per-segment record as written to the TMS-like export for human review.

qa_status.description: Outcome of automated QA checks for this segment.

qa_issues.description: List of machine-detected issues for this segment.

glossary_applied.description: Whether a glossary was applied or attempted for this segment.

run_id.description: Foreign key linking the segment to a run_record.run_id.
